data.sampling_design: Controlled reporting exercise over the31 archived trees, not a documented original field-sampling design. Partition the fixed finite population before sampling by its recorded diameter: small has diameter<=12 inches,large has diameter>12. Independently within each stratum,assume simple random sampling without replacement at the stated fixed sample size. The stored sample is one reproducible draw: NumPy default_rng(440),small then large,choice without replacement from ascending original row IDs. All sampled volumes are original readings. The population for inference is exactly these31 archived units,not all trees in a forest.
data.reporting_target: Estimate the finite-population mean timber volume per tree using the stated sampling design and known stratum sizes. Report its plug-in design standard error using within-stratum unbiased sample variances and the without-replacement finite-population corrections. Compare the ordinary mean of all sampled readings with the design estimate by pooled-minus-design difference. Report standard error,not standard deviation of tree volumes or a confidence-interval width. There is no nonresponse,weight trimming,calibration model,normal-coverage guarantee or superpopulation inference.
data.unit_definitions: Volume is cubic feet of timber per tree. The original field called Girth is actually diameter in inches,as documented by R. This sample export names it diameter_inches; stratum membership is fixed before sampling.
